title: Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials Enable Accurate Metal-Organic Framework Molecular Modeling
experiments_summary: The study introduces MOFSimBench, a benchmarking framework evaluating 19 universal machine learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) plus MACE-MP-MOF0 and UFF4MOF on a curated set of 100 nanoporous structures drawn from QMOF, MOSAEC-DB, IZA, and CURATED-COF databases. Four main experimental tasks were performed: (1) Structural optimization: atom positions and cell parameters were simultaneously relaxed using the FrechetCellFilter and LBFGS optimizer in ASE, with a force convergence criterion of 1e-3 eV/Å or a maximum of 5,000 steps; UFF4MOF used LAMMPS with the conjugate gradient minimizer. Relative volume differences versus DFT-optimized structures and convergence rates were recorded. (2) Molecular dynamics (MD) stability: simulations were run in the NpT ensemble at 300 K and 1 bar for 50 ps using a 1 fs timestep and the ASE IsotropicMKTNPT driver. Structures were first minimized (LBFGS, 1e-3 eV/Å or 1,000 steps), velocities initialized from a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution at 300 K, equilibrated in NVT with Langevin dynamics (friction 0.01 fs^-1) for 1 ps, then subjected to the 50 ps NpT production run. Volume deviations between initial and final configurations were used to assess stability. (3) Bulk modulus prediction: structures were fully optimized (LBFGS, 1e-3 eV/Å or 1,000 steps), then volumetric strains of ±4% were applied in 11 evenly spaced steps, each re-optimized with the FIRE optimizer. The bulk modulus was extracted by fitting a Birch-Murnaghan equation of state. Structures with EOS volume minima deviating more than 1% from the initial optimization minimum were excluded as failed. DFT reference bulk moduli were computed with CP2K v9.1 using PBE+D3(BJ), GTH pseudopotentials, DZVP-MOLOPT-SR basis sets, and an 800 Ry plane-wave cutoff, with ±4% volumetric strain in 5 steps and atomic position optimization at each strain, managed via AiiDA and the Cp2KMultistageWorkChain workflow. (4) Heat capacity prediction: structures were first optimized (LBFGS, 1e-3 eV/Å or 1,000 steps), then harmonic phonon calculations were performed using Phonopy with no supercells, finite differences of 0.01 Å, and a phonon mesh of 100; heat capacity at 300 K was extracted. DFT reference heat capacities and structures were sourced from Moosavi et al. (2022). All uMLIP calculations incorporated D3 dispersion corrections, either pre-trained (orb-d3-v2, MACE-MP-MOF0) or applied at inference time via torch-dftd with PBE damping (BJ) and a 40 Bohr cutoff. Model performance was compared across architectures (equivariant GNNs, graph transformers, GNS, graph basis function networks) and training datasets (MPtrj, Alexandria, OMat24, proprietary), including analysis of conservative versus non-conservative force prediction and the effect of fine-tuning on MOF-specific data.
